short: A six-day blaze destroyed much of Rome and fed lasting rumours that Nero himself was to blame.
full:
On 19 July 64 CE, a fire broke out among shops near the Circus Maximus and spread through Rome's densely packed insulae for six days, subsided, then flared again for three more. Of the city's fourteen regions, three were levelled and seven badly damaged; only four escaped untouched. Nero was at Antium when the fire began and returned to organise relief, opening his gardens to the homeless and shipping in grain from Ostia, but rumour held that he had started the blaze to clear ground for himself, or watched it burn for inspiration.

Tacitus records that Nero shifted blame onto Rome's Christian community, who were rounded up and executed as scapegoats. The burned centre of the city was rebuilt to a stricter code, with wider streets and fire-breaks, and part of it was absorbed into Nero's own building programme, which only deepened suspicion that the fire had served him.
